notes.title: Update on July 24
notes.notes:
Hi everyone, Yi Xian will be updated at 14:00, July 24. Please pay attention to the update time, avoiding affect your match.

1.Card adjustment

Sword Intent Surge：no cost Qi

Dev notes:

· The Sword Intent deck heavily relies on the level of Cloud Dance Rhythm to gain Qi. With this adjustment, we aim to make Sword Surge more flexible, allowing it to integrate smoothly into decks even without a high-level Cloud Dance Rhythm.

Crash Fist - Styx Night ：no cost HP→ cost 3 HP；gain 2/3/4→3/4/5 Styx

Dev notes:

· During initial internal testing, we found that Crash Fist - Styx Night's synergy with Crash Citta-Dharma (when cost HP) was overly powerful, so it was nerfed to become the only Crash Fist without costing HP. However, as the meta changes, Styx Night has fallen behind compared to other immortal fates. This buff aims to restore its competitiveness while realigning it with the core mechanic of HP cost for Crash Fist.

M - Five Elements Circulation：Qi +2/2/3→2/3/4

Dev notes:

· Previously, Du Lingyuan's M - Five Elements Cycle was particularly strong when paired with Fire Spirit - Blazing Wildfire for quick damage and Metal Spirit - Iron Bone for flexible defense, making the deck well-rounded and overpowered. However, after the last adjustment (activating only one Element type), the strategy became more dependent on Innate Element, significantly increasing its difficulty.

Since standard Wood Spirit - Dark Fragrance decks have remained balanced in performance, we've decided to revert the earlier Qi adjustments for M-Five Elements Cycle.

M - Magnanimous Righteousness：Agility +4→6

Dev notes:

· M - Magnanimous Righteousness was designed to bridge the Crash Fist and debuff cards, allowing players to better utilize cards from both systems. However, based on observations, the limited Agility it provided made it difficult to incorporate into optimized deck builds. Therefore, we've decided to strengthen this card.

2.Immortal Fate adjustments

Dragon Scale：remove 10 Destiny

· Dragon Scale’s +10 Destiny was originally introduced during the Life Shop season, as the season mechanics at the time heavily penalized Destiny, making the Dragon Scale significantly underperform. To compensate, it received this buff.

In subsequent versions, Dragon Scale remained a reliable top-4 pick, and since it didn’t disrupt overall balance, we opted to leave it unchanged. However, in the current mirage season, the card has become overly strong due to new season mechanics, drawing widespread criticism from the community. As a result, we’ve decided to revert this adjustment.

Best Choice: gain 3 Exchange chances

· Best Choice may appear powerful at first glance, but it has actually been a "trap option". Selecting it disrupts breakthrough pacing compared to choosing Cultivation, and its deck-completion boost is weaker than The Way of Adaptation from the Virtuoso Phase (which gives +8 exchange chances). This is because a complete deck requires a cohesive set of cards, not just random cards from current phase.

However, Best Choice does outperform The Way of Adaptation after Round 16, when upgrading Lv.2/3 Incarnation cards becomes crucial for deck.

With this adjustment, we've improved its early-game value, aiming to transform Best Choice from a trap into a strategic decision — one that players can weigh based on their Cultivation progress and deck needs.

Hi everyone, Yi Xian will be updated at 14:00, May 29 (UTC+8). Please pay attention to the update time.

Balancement:
· M - Ruthless Water: cost 1 Qi; no long take effect on Styx

Dev note:
M - Ruthless Water has relatively high strength when paired with Weaken Fulu and Disturbing Fulu in the Immortality Phase, increasing Qi cost to create more room for opponent strategy. The trigger condition for the continuous effect has been adjusted to align with Astral Eclipse.

· M - Incessant: Gain 3/4/5→2/3/4 Regeneration

Dev note:
M - Incessant has high single-card strength in the early stages of the Incarnation Phase. In the later stages, multiple M - Incessants combined with Predicament for Immortals can suppress many decks with weaker sustained combat capabilities. As a result, its base stats have been nerfed.

Dev note:
Adjusted to require only 2 Spirit Swords for chase, increasing deck flexibility.

· M - Wood Spirit Recovery: Restore your HP to what it was at the start of your last turn (up to 15)

Dev note:
In the late game, M - Wood Spirit Recovery provides excessive healing when positioned correctly, making it difficult to counter. As a result, a cap has been implemented.

· M - Exercise Bones: HP +5→0
Dev note:
M - Exercise Bones performs strongly in the Immortality Phase when growth-focused decks are less prevalent, so its base stats have been reduced.

· M - Sinking Qi: HP+4 → 9/10/11
Dev note:
M - Sinking Qi requires significant Agility and Qi, making it difficult to play effectively during transition stage. To improve its viability, its HP has been increased.

Based on usage rates and win rates, we have made adjustments to the lower-usage Divinity Phase cards in order to improve their performance.

Over the past week, the meta has gone through multiple changes, driven by your innovation. Xuan-Yuan Sword initially dominated, but it was soon surpassed by the  Kunlun Mirror + Pi Yun Zhui Yue. Then, Donghuang Zhong with Water Spirit - Dive emerged as a strong counter, leading to a more versatile strategy. The meta continued to evolve, with the introduction of combos such as Yao Ling combined with Hexagram Formacide or Internal Injury to counter Dive, as well as higher-damage builds like Donghuang Zhong + Unrestrained Sword or Sword Intent to quickly eliminate the slower water deck. Additionally, Spirit Fusion Pot began to see more use as a counter to Donghuang Zhong, despite its initially low appearance rate, as some players found it highly effective.

3.Balance adjustments:
(1) Mind-Body Resonance (Ji Fangsheng, Foundation Phase)
Before adjustment: Whenever you gain 1 Physique in battle, you gain 1 DEF. Add 1 Physique after each battle (not exceeding the cap).
After adjustment: Whenever you gain 1 Physique in battle, you gain 1 DEF.

After this adjustment, Ji Fangsheng will rely more on players’ flexible use of lower-phase cards to get through the early stages, then unleash full power in the mid-to-late game.            

Ji Fangsheng is set to have deep and immeasurable cultivation and power. During design, we made him the fastest to break through to the incarnation phase to reflect his profound cultivation. Additionally, we gave him powerful mid-to-late game exclusive moves to showcase his unpredictable strength. However, for balance, we made it so that Ji Fangsheng can only increase his physique cap by winning battles. During internal testing, opinions on his power were polarized — some thought he was too strong, while others felt he was too weak. 

In the first week after release, Ji Fangsheng ranked the lowest in both average rank and win rate, mainly due to a lack of deck and his less reliable physique cultivation compared to other characters. We strengthened Mind-Body Resonance at the time to stabilize his cultivation. With subsequent environmental changes and continuous development of Ji Fangsheng’s deck by high-level players, his average rank and win rate gradually improved, reaching above average in the 3000+ matchers, and ranking at the highest level in the top 1% of matches.

We want to keep Ji Fangsheng’s unique deck while balancing him, so after multiple considerations and comparisons, we decided to first roll back the Mind-Body Resonance enhancement while leaving his exclusive moves unchanged for now.

We will continue to monitor Ji Fangsheng’s performance and make further adjustments if necessary.

(2) Birdie Wind (Tan Shuyan, Virtuoso Phase)
Before adjustment: Add 1 DEF for each time your HP changes.
After adjustment: Randomly gain 1 card that adds HP; add 1 DEF each time your HP changes.

Cards that add HP in the Virtuoso phase and below include: Incessant, Mountain Hexagram, Stillness Citta-Dharma, Imposing, Yin Yang Formation, Qi Therapy, Hunter Becomes Preyer.

Tan Shuyan needs to carefully plan card upgrade in the early stages to trigger Study Hard and ensure timely breakthroughs. Therefore, more players tend to choose draw or cultivation-related immortal fates in the Virtuoso phase to supplement cultivation, preserving more cards for breakthroughs. 

Even when playing healing-based decks, Birdie Wind was often chosen only when no cultivation-boosting immortal fates were available. This adjustment aims to make healing decks more inclined to choose Birdie Wind, while providing a stable choice for Virtuoso phase across other decks.

Early combos like “Musician-Tan Shuyan” and “Painter-Tan Shuyan” were criticized by many players for negatively impacting player experience and game duration, leading to gradual weakening of these mechanics. After healing decks fell out of favor, Birdie Wind has consistently been the least chosen ability for Tan Shuyan. 

We are aware that if healing decks become too dominant, they could recreate past negative experiences, so we have been cautious with Birdie Wind. This season’s fusion card, Traces Revitalized, aims to make healing decks more offensive rather than dragging out time, while giving them a strong counter-attack capability. In our internal testing, Tan Shuyan’s deck paired with the Fortune Teller had a high win rate in the late game. 

However, based on the actual post-release performance, transition instability remains an issue, exacerbated by the Furnace of Void’s relic mechanics. This adjustment attempts to enhance Tan Shuyan’s transitional abilities, and we will continue to monitor the ladder performance of healing decks.

Cat Teaser：Exchange Card Chance +3/6/12→1/2/4

Dev: Curiosity makes players reluctant to use it, feeling like it wastes the Exchange Card Chance in some situations,. But how can a cat resist? Therefore, we've made it so that Curiosity no longer wastes the Exchange Card Chance and introduced a playful mechanic that makes the cat unable to resist triggering Curiosity continuously. As Curiosity now provides Exchange Card Chance, the Cat Teaser has been adjusted to a standard level and is no longer compensating for the consumption of Exchange Card Chances by Curiosity.

Dev: Before the last adjustment, Soul Seizing was relatively dominant in lower MMR segments, while in higher MMR segments, it did not significantly outperform other decks. Therefore, we weakened Unwavering Soul at that time and continued to observe. After the last adjustment, the usage rate and win rate of Realm-Killing Palms have normalized, but both Soul Seizing and the usage of Force combos have increased across all MMR segments. Hence, we have decided to further adjust Debuff combos and Force combos. Additionally, to increase the diversity of the meta, we have strengthened some characters with lower usage rates, hoping to bring more variety.

Balance adjustments are an ongoing and dynamic process. As new decks are created and player skill levels improve, perspectives on balance changes. We will keep track of changes in the meta and make adjustments accordingly. Moreover, data is not the sole criterion; cold data can not fully capture the true gaming experience. Even cards with average win rates should be adjusted if they significantly impact the gaming experience. After all, playing games is about having a fun experience, not just achieving balance based on data. Therefore, we encourage everyone to provide timely feedback on real gaming experiences, as well as any bugs or issues encountered through Discord, TapTap, QQ, to help us understand more perspectives and content beyond data and make Divine Chess more enjoyable together.

We found that some players were matched together and deliberately played each other to reduce the damage of Destiny, which affected the fairness of the game.

 An email warning upon the first time.
 1000 RANK POINTS will be deducted for each offence after the warning, and you will not be able to see who your opponent is for 72 hours.
[/olist]
You can join our Discord and DM the Administrator CocoLa03 and provide relevant evidence (screenshots or video recordings). The in-game reporting system will be available at the end of Early access.

0.2.0 version update:

1. New contents test
Cloud Spirit Sword Guild and QiXing Tower both add 4 new cards ( these testing cards have not yet completed gameplay and balance evaluations. So maybe they may be modified, redone or deleted at any time. Besides, art resources are tempory resouces, and the official ones will be drawn after the card effect is determined.)
Add one new general Destiny. Cloud Spirit Sword Guild and QiXing Tower both add 2 new unique Destinies.
Some cards and Destiny values have been adjusted. Due to there are much adjustments, so they are not listed. You can check them in the Card Book.

2. New mechanisms tests:
The upper limit of the chances to switch cards is 20 now. (the chances is allowed to temporarily exceed the upper limit during the cultivating process. Only after entering the next battle, the part exceeding the upper limit will be cleared)
In order to increase the operational space in the later stage and balance the dilution of the newly added cards to the card pool, the chance to switch cards will increase according to the round.
Round 1-9: 3 times (same as the last version)
Round 10-14: 4 times (plus 1 time)
Round 15-19: 5 times (plus 2 times)
Round 20 and more: 6 times(plus 3 times)

In addition, the first card switch in each round will get an bonus: increase the probability of getting your own realm card. The specific algorithm may be adjusted and will not be announced during the testing period.

3.  UI adjustments of cards:
The lvl 2 card adds a small gem, which is different from the level 1 card.
A small dot is added at the bottom of the card UI to represent the realm (every additional dot represents a higher realm) to help players who have difficulty identifying the card realm.
